page: Microsoft Azure M128ps_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance provides 128 dedicated virtual processor cores and 1,388.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 10.84 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server contains no integrated GPUs.

The instance configuration does not include local disk storage, requiring external attached volumes such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent file systems and operating system disks. Because it operates on an arm64 processor platform, application environments must support ARM instruction sets. The high memory density provides significant capacity per core, while the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent compute performance without virtualization contention from shared cores.

The M128ps_v4 instance is targeted at memory-intensive enterprise workloads that require extensive contiguous RAM spaces on ARM architectures. Common deployment scenarios include in-memory databases, large-scale data caching tiers, high-volume transactional database management systems, and distributed analytics engines requiring extensive working memory.
description: Microsoft Azure M128ps_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for high-memory workloads on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance features 128 dedicated vCPUs paired with 1,388.0 GB of memory, delivering approximately 10.84 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes no integrated GPUs and provides no local ephemeral disk storage, requiring workloads to rely on remote storage solutions such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent I/O operations. The dedicated core allocation ensures predictable execution without multitenant CPU contention, while the ARM-based compute engine offers high resource density for software stacks compiled for arm64. Due to its large memory footprint and high core count, the M128ps_v4 is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, in-memory analytics engines, and enterprise backend applications requiring substantial RAM capacity.
